BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL PASO                        )
ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF ITS RETAIL                        )   Docket No. 25-00082-UT
ELECTRIC RATES PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE                           )
NO. 317                                                            )

      THE CITY OF LAS CRUCES’ MOTION FOR AN ORDER COMPELLING
          EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY TO PROVIDE RESPONSES
     TO THE CITY’S NINTH SET OF INTERROGATORIES, REQUESTS FOR
      PRODUCTION OF DOCUMENTS, AND REQUESTS FOR ADMISSIONS
    AND ORDERING EXPEDITED RESPONSES TO THIS MOTION TO COMPEL

       COMES NOW the City of Las Cruces (the “City” or “CLC”), by and through the

undersigned attorneys, and pursuant to 1.2.2.25(J) NMAC and 1.2.2.12(C)(1)(e) NMAC, moves

the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (the “NMPRC” or “Commission”) compelling El

Paso Electric Company’s (“Company” or “EPE”) to provide responses to the City’s Ninth Set of

Interrogatories, Requests for Production of Documents, and Requests for Admissions, which were

served upon EPE on August 5, 2026. As explained below, the City believes that responses were

due on August 20, 2026, or 15 days after they were served, while EPE believes that discovery was

tolled by the Sua Sponte Order Vacating Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and

Requiring the Filing of an Amended Application (“Sua Sponte Order”) issued on July 16, 2026,

and that the responses were due on or before September 8, 2026. In either case, EPE has failed to

provide any responses to the CLC Discovery Requests. Due to the simple nature of this request

and the pressing procedural schedule in this matter, the City requests that the Commission order

EPE to file its response no later than September 14, 2026.

       As grounds for this motion, the City states:

       1.      The Sua Sponte Order, issued on July 16, 2026, required EPE to file an amended

application for revision of its rates on or before August 6, 2026. See Sua Sponte Order ¶ E.
         2.       The Sua Sponte Order vacated the procedural schedule established by the

Procedural Order issued on April 26, 2026, “including all testimony, prehearing hearing, and

related deadlines.” Id. ¶ A.

        3.       The Sua Sponte Order tolled all pending deadlines for motions or responses to

motions. See id. ¶ B.

        4.       The Sua Sponte Order did not place this entire case in abeyance. See Sua Sponte

Order, passim.

        5.       The Sua Sponte Order did not otherwise order a stay of discovery. See Sua Sponte

Order, passim.

        6.       The Sua Sponte Order stated that “[t]he vacatur and stay of procedural deadlines

ordered herein do not relieve EPE of its continuing obligation to respond completely and

accurately to outstanding discovery or to supplement prior responses as required by Commission

rule. Sua Sponte Order ¶ J(8).

        7.       The City served its Ninth Set of Interrogatories, Requests for Production of

Documents, and Requests for Admissions 1 (“CLC Discovery Requests”) on August 5, 2026.

Pursuant to Rule 1.2.2.25(J)(2), a complete copy of the CLC Discovery Requests is attached to

this motion as Exhibit A.

        8.       As shown in Exhibit A, the CLC Discovery Requests concerned a variety of cost

items arising from EPE’s claimed book amounts, previous discovery responses, and in a few

instances the changes to EPE’s cost of service discussed in its Second Notice of Errata and Filing




1
  The City previously had served three sets of requests for production of documents and eight sets of
interrogatories, requests for production of documents, and requests for admissions on EPE. The Company has
numbered its sets of responses consecutively, regardless of the type of discovery requests and the City’s
numbering. Therefore, in EPE’s view, the CLC Discovery Requests are the City’s twelfth set of discovery
requests.
                                                    2
 of Replacement Exhibits, which was filed on July 7, 2026, and which precipitated the Sua Sponte

Order.

         9.     Under Rule 1.2.2.25(E)(3), 1.2.2.25(F)(5), and 1.2.2.25(G)(2) NMAC, EPE’s

responses to the CLC Discovery Requests were due within 15 days of service, or on August 20,

2026.

         10.    EPE did not serve responses to the CLC Discovery Requests on August 20, 2026.

         11.    On August 31, 2026, counsel for the City sent an email message to seven attorneys

representing EPE in this Docket No. 25-00082-UT, notifying the Company that the City believed

EPE was already 11 days behind in the deadline for responding to the CLC Discovery Requests

and asking EPE to provide an intended response date by no later than September 1, 2024. See

Email Message from Stevens to EPE Counsel dated August 31, 2026, at 1:55 PM, attached hereto

as Exhibit B.

         12.    At 4:51 PM on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, EPE counsel Jeffrey Wechsler replied

to the City’s email message expressing an interpretation of the Sua Sponte Order as a stay of

discovery, as well as “all procedural deadlines in this docket”). See Email Message from Wechsler

to Stevens dated September 1, 2026, at 4:51 PM, attached hereto as Exhibit C. Mr. Wechsler stated

EPE’s interpretation that “the stay was lifted on August 27th” when the Order Establishing Revised

Procedural Order and Addressing Outstanding Motions was issued, so service of the CLC

Discovery Requests became effective on that day and by rule the responses were due on September

8, 2026.

         13.    Counsel for the City replied to counsel for EPE on September 2, 2026, stating that

it would not be productive to discuss the timing of EPE’s responses to the CLC Discovery Requests

provided that they actually were received on Tuesday, September 8, 2026. See Email message



                                                3
 from Stevens to Wechsler, et al. dated September 2, 2026, at 8:37 AM, attached hereto as Exhibit

D.

       14.     The City disagrees with EPE’s interpretation of the Sua Sponte Order. Compare

Ex. B with Ex. C; see also supra ¶¶ 2-6.

       15.     The City disagrees with EPE’s understanding of the Hearing Examiners’ position

regarding discovery during the scheduling conference held on August 25, 2026. See Ex. C. At

the beginning of the discussion of outstanding motions, including the City’s motion to compel

complete responses to its first and second requests for production of documents, Hearing Examiner

Gedko remarked that most likely, discovery has continued, then asked whether there was a need

to update the City’s outstanding motion to compel.

       16.     It has become necessary for the Commission to rule on the correct interpretation of

the Sua Sponte Order, although EPE has failed to comply with its discovery obligations as reflected

in Mr. Wechsler’s email message attached as Exhibit C. The Commission’s interpretation is

relevant to determining appropriate sanctions for EPE’s failure to provide discovery responses,

including modifications to the current procedural schedule in this case.

       17.   The City did not receive any responses to the CLC Discovery Requests on September

8, 2026.

       18.     The City did not receive any responses to the CLC Discovery Requests by the close

of business on September 9, 2026.

       19.      The City believes that EPE’s practice of serving partial responses to discovery

requests on the date that responses are due, as indicated by Mr. Wechsler’s email message of

September 1, 2026, violates both the letter and the intent of Rule 1.2.2.25 NMAC and of discovery

practice generally. Cf. Ex. C (“We are working on responses to the City’s 12th Set of Discovery

now, and will have timely responses beginning on September 8th.”) (emphasis added). The City

                                                4
 is aware of no precedent from this Commission, or in case law from New Mexico or other

jurisdictions, that allows a party to “begin” serving discovery responses on the date that they are

due and to continue providing portions of the responses to a single set of discovery requests at that

party’s leisure thereafter, unless the party propounding the discovery requests and the party

responding to those discovery requests agree to such a schedule in advance of the deadline. Cf.

Procedural Order ¶ R (Apr. 27, 2026) (“Agreements between or among any of the participants

regarding discovery matters is encouraged.”)

       20.      The City attempted to discuss a potential resolution of EPE’s failure to respond to

the CLC Discovery Requests even by its own stated deadline, by calling EPE attorney Wechsler

at 11:45 a.m. on September 10, 2026. He did not answer the call at that time and did not respond

to voice messages left at that time. After leaving voice messages for both Mr. Wechsler and EPE

attorney Kari Olson at 2:06 p.m. on September 10, 2026, Ms. Olson called counsel for the City

and expressed the opinion that EPE intended to serve responses on September 11, 2026, based on

how the Company calendared the deadline from the date of issuance of the Order Establishing

Revised Procedural Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions on August 27, 2026. Ms. Olson

agreed to call counsel for the City again after receiving a draft of this motion, which she was aware

that the City intended to file by the close of business on September 10, 2026.

       21.      At 4:21 p.m. on September 10, 2026, Ms. Olson called counsel for the City and

announced that the Company opposes the motion to compel, counted September 11, 2026 as 15

days from the date of the August 28, 2026 order, and intends to begin serving responses on August

11, 2026, with further responses on September 14, 2026 and September 15, 2026.

       22.      In light of the Company’s representation in Exhibit C that it would have the

discovery responses by September 8, 2026, the City requests that the Commission: (1) order EPE

to file an expedited written response to this motion no later than September 14, 2026; (2) grant this

                                                 5
 motion and order EPE to file complete responses to the CLC Discovery Requests by no later than

Wednesday, September 16, 2026; and (3) modify the Order Establishing Revised Procedural

Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions to extend the deadline for the filing of Staff and

intervenor direct testimony to no earlier than November 4, 2026, and the deadline for rebuttal

testimony to November 23, 2026.

       23.     The proposed revision to the current deadline for Staff and intervenor direct

testimony represents a mere eight business days after the current deadline of October 23, 2026.

That revised deadline would enable the Commission to retain the current deadline for rebuttal

testimony of November 20, 2026. Unfortunately, however, these revised deadlines also would

reward EPE’s refusal to answer CLC’s Discovery Requests within the time allowed after the

Company was served with that discovery on August 5, 2026, by giving EPE 27 days to respond in

addition to the 15 days allowed by Rule 1.2.2.25 NMAC. Another alternative, consistent with the

Joint Motion for Clarification and Reconsideration of Order Establishing Revised Procedural

Schedule and Order Extending Suspension Period for Advice Notice No. 317, filed by the City

and other intervenors on September 8, 2026, would be to recognize that the suspension period for

this case began running at the time EPE’s Amended Application for Revision of Retail Electric

Rates was filed on August 6, 2026, and to modify the entire procedural schedule.

       24.     As indicated by the foregoing information and the exhibits to this motion, the City

and EPE have made a good faith effort to resolve this dispute but have been unable to do so.

       25.    In accordance with Rule 1.2.2.12(E) NMAC, the City has attempted to ascertain

whether this motion will be opposed. EPE opposes the motion. The Coalition for Clean

Affordable Energy (“CCAE”), Doña Ana County, and pro se intervenor Dwight Eggers support

this motion. Walmart, Inc. takes no position on the motion. The City did not receive responses

from the Public Interest Advocacy Staff (“Staff”) of the NMPRC, Western Resource Advocates

                                               6
 (“WRA”), the New Mexico Department of Justice (“NMDOJ”), the Department of Defense and

All Other Federal Executive Agencies (“DOD/FEA”), New Mexico State University (“NMSU”),

or pro se intervenors Stephen Fischmann and Philip B. Simpson prior to filing this motion.

       WHEREFORE, the City of Las Cruces respectively asks the Commission to order

expedited responses to this motion, above; to issue an order compelling EPE to fully respond to

the CLC Discovery Requests, above; and to modify the deadlines for Staff and intervenor direct

testimony and rebuttal testimony, all as set out in Paragraph 22, above.

                                         DEFINITIONS

      1.      EPE/you/your. The term “EPE,” “you,” or “your” refers to El Paso Electric
Company and includes, but is not limited to all of its attorneys, officers, consultants, agents,
employees, directors, representatives, officials, departments, or divisions.

      2.      Commission or NMPRC. The term “Commission” or “NMPRC” means the New
Mexico Public Regulation Commission and its predecessor agency.

       3.      City or CLC. The term “City” or “CLC” refers to the City of Las Cruces.

        4.      Communication. The term “communication” is to be construed broadly and
includes but is not limited to any oral statement, dialogue, telephone conversation, colloquy,
discussion, or conversation and any transfer of thought or ideas between persons electronically or
by means of documents, including any transfer of data from one location to another by electronic
or similar means.

        5.     Correspondence. The term “correspondence” includes all letters, telegrams,
notices, messages, or other written or electronic communications or memoranda, or other records
of conversations, meetings, conferences or other oral communications.

        6.      Document/documentation. The term “document” or “documentation” means any
paper, book, record, or any expression recorded, stored, or reproduced in any medium, including,
without limitation, a medium such as computer disks, computer tapes, computer memory or other
computer storage devices, film, microfiche or microfilm from which information may be retrieved
electronically or through other means, and shall include all written, graphic, photographic matter
and all audio records, however produced or reproduced, of every kind and description, in your
actual or constructive possession, custody, or control, including originals, all copies, drafts, and
versions. By way of example, but not limitation, the term “document” shall include all contracts,
agreements, correspondence, resolutions, amendments, invoices, telegrams, notes, minutes, or
audio or video records of any type of personal or telephone conversations or of meetings or
conferences, press releases, studies, memoranda, analyses, reports, and project files, or reports
similar to any of the foregoing, however denominated, and includes materials within the scope of
Rule 1-034(A) NMRA of the New Mexico Rules of Civil Procedure for the District Courts.



                                                 2
        7.       Explain. The term “explain” means to make known in detail, to make clear the
cause or reason of and account for each act, omission, incident, event, condition, circumstance,
decision and/or thing related directly or indirectly to the subject of the explanation, including all
pertinent dates.

         8.    FERC. The term “FERC” means the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

        9.      Identify (With Respect to Persons). When referring to a person, “to identify” means
to give, to the extent known, the person’s full name, present or last known address, the present or
last known place of employment. Once a person has been identified in accordance with this
subparagraph, only the name of that person need be listed in response to subsequent discovery
requesting the identification of that person.

        10.    Identify (With Respect to Documents). When referring to documents, “to identify”
means to give, to the extent known, the (I) type of document; (ii) general subject matter; (iii) date
of the document; and (iv) author(s), addressee(s), and recipient(s).

         11.      Identify (With Respect to Communications). When referring to communications,
“identify” means to state the date or dates upon which the communication occurred, the person
initiating the communication, each other person who participated in the communication, the
subject matter of the communication and the nature of the communication (e.g., memo, telephone
call, etc.); and to identify each other person who observed or has knowledge of the communication,
the person from whom or the manner in which you learned of the communication, the date you
learned of the communication, and each document which reflects, refers to, or in any way relates
to such communication.

         12.   Number. The use of the singular form of any word includes the plural and vice
versa.

        13.     Person. The term “person” means any natural person or any business, legal or
governmental entity or association, including profit and non-profit corporations, associations,
partnerships, limited liability companies, and municipal corporations or any other entity having
legal identity and status.

         14.   PUCT. The term “PUCT” means the Public Utility Commission of Texas.


                                        INSTRUCTIONS

     1.     Interrogatories, Requests for Admissions, and Requests for Production of
Documents must be answered with particularity and in detail.

       2.      Each response must be signed by the person or persons upon whose personal
knowledge the response is based and/or who helped in any way in formulating the response.
Additionally, please identify each witness who may testify concerning the matters contained in
each response or document produced.

        3.      In making your responses, you must produce all relevant documents and data by
attachment or by identifying the documents previously produced which relate to your answers.
You must also clearly identify each Interrogatory to which the document relates, and your answer
should identify specific pages, tables, exhibits, etc. within each document that are relevant to your
response.

       4.     These Interrogatories, Requests for Production of Documents, and Requests for
Admissions are continuing in nature and in the event information provided in a response is changed
or supplemented by future developments or other factors, you must amend or supplement it.
